deep.reconstruction:
The page closes Euler's preface and opens the 'First Method'. In the preface Euler says the investigations come from his correspondence with Goldbach and are 'for the most part' to be credited to Goldbach's acuteness. He announces three quite different methods for the series of the previous page, namely S(m,n) = Σ_{k≥1} k^{-m} Σ_{j≤k} j^{-n}.

§1 states a general lemma. Let t = Σ_{i≥0} a_i and u = Σ_{i≥0} α_i, with a_0 = α_0 = 1, and let v = Σ a_i α_i be the diagonal series. Then

Σ_i a_i (α_0+…+α_i) + Σ_i α_i (a_0+…+a_i) = t·u + v.

The reason is that the two left-hand sums together contain every product a_i α_j once. The only exception is the diagonal products a_i α_i, which appear twice; since t·u contains them only once, v must be added.

In modern terms, Σ_{j≤i} + Σ_{i≤j} equals the full double sum plus the diagonal. This is the 'stuffle' (harmonic-product) decomposition of a product of two sums.

The next page applies it with a_i = (i+1)^{-m} and α_i = (i+1)^{-n}. This gives the reflection relation ζ*(m,n) + ζ*(n,m) = ζ(m)ζ(n) + ζ(m+n) for the non-strict ('star') double zeta values. The problem served is evaluating Euler–Goldbach double sums from known single zeta values.
errors: No mathematical error. Tacitly, absolute convergence of the series is needed so that the double sum can be rearranged; Euler does not state this.
Printed typo 'fecudae' for 'fecundae' in the original.

ideas.what: Product of two series split into the two 'triangular' sums of terms times partial sums of the other series, with a diagonal correction: Σ a_i A'_i + Σ α_i A_i = tu + v.
ideas.modern_name: Stuffle / quasi-shuffle (harmonic) product; inclusion–exclusion on the diagonal of a double sum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (and Goldbach), correspondence 1742–43 and E477; formalized as the quasi-shuffle algebra by Hoffman (1990s)
ideas.where_published: E477 itself (Novi Comm. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 20, 1776; Opera Omnia I.15); also the Euler–Goldbach letters of 1742–43

ideas.what: Attribution of the double-series investigations largely to Goldbach
ideas.modern_name: Historical priority of the Euler–Goldbach double zeta (Euler sums) work
ideas.where_published: E477 preface; Euler–Goldbach correspondence (edited by Fuss 1843; Lemmermeyer & Mattmüller 2015)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known stuffle/reflection lemma behind ζ(m,n)+ζ(n,m)=ζ(m)ζ(n)+ζ(m+n). It is widely cited as Euler's (and Goldbach's) in the multiple-zeta-value literature, so nothing here is new.
transcription_corrections: 'secudae' in the transcription faithfully reproduces the printed typo 'fecudae' (for 'fecundae').
The previous-page 'coluerum' should read 'colueram'; this is unsure from the image, since the previous page was not inspected.
'S 3' at the foot of the page is a printer's signature mark, not mathematics.
